back: Open stomata let CO₂ in for photosynthesis but let water vapour out.
Kidney-shaped, chloroplasts, thick inner wall, radial microfibrils, many proton pumps and K⁺ channels.
Proton pumps (ATP) → K⁺ in → ψ falls → water in by osmosis → turgid → bow apart.
K⁺ and anions out → ψ rises → water out → flaccid → pore closes.
Plant growth regulator produced in water stress that closes stomata.
Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) in the guard cell cytoplasm.

front: When do stomata open and close?
back: Open: light, low internal CO₂. Close: dark, high CO₂, water stress (ABA).
Open after dawn, may partly close at midday in water stress, close in the evening; an internal clock helps time it.
